headline: Report: Canadiens' Prospects Hage, Zharovsky 'Will Be Available' To The Team At The End Of The Season
take:
The Hockey News reports that Canadiens prospects Michael Hage and Alexander Zharovsky "will be available" to Montreal at the end of the season, citing Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman.

For a team sitting at 11-3-3 with 25 points through 17 games, that is a pleasant problem to have, but our numbers say the current group is not as dominant as the record suggests. MTL holds 49.1 percent of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality, so it tracks who is creating the better chances) so far this season, a hair below even. The record owes a lot to goaltending: MTL's goalies have saved 6.6 goals above expected, meaning they have stopped far more than the quality of shots faced would predict. At five-on-five the share improves to 52 percent, which is a healthier sign, and the power play (0.59 expected goals per game) and penalty kill (0.9 allowed per game) are middling rather than elite.

That is why added young talent at the end of the year matters. A team winning on hot goaltending has little margin if the saves normalize, and two prospects who can push the chance-creation side would help most.
